chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ubeyda al-Hazza', who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever builds a mosque, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.'

Abu Ubeyda said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me on the road to Mecca, and I had leveled out a mosque with stones. So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We hope that this will be from that.' So he said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for building a mosque in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the spiritual merit of mosque construction, a practice deeply rooted in Shia tradition as an act of communal worship and social cohesion. The personal confirmation by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to Abu Ubaydah highlights the authenticity of the promise, linking physical effort in establishing a place of prayer to eternal reward. This narrative reinforces the concept of 'Bayt' (house) not merely as a structure, but as a divine abode prepared in Jannah for the devout builder.
